results.alertTitle: AWS console sign-in by jane.smith from an external address

summary.tpReason: The Jane event is a successful AWS ConsoleLogin with MFA and is paired with successful AWS CLI discovery calls; if the telemetry were production-real it could represent use of valid credentials. However, the purported external source is an RFC 5737 documentation address, and the surrounding AWS records use multiple TEST-NET addresses and overtly synthetic identifiers, strongly indicating lab/test data rather than hostile Jane activity.
summary.fpReason: 198.51.100.22 belongs to 198.51.100.0/24 (TEST-NET-2), reserved for documentation rather than public routing (RFC 5737). Jane's only 30-day AWS activity is six successful MFA-authenticated events from that same address between 16:51 and 17:20, with routine read-only discovery and no changes, persistence, or data-object reads. This is consistent with a simulated/expected session that triggered an over-broad 'external address' rule.
summary.whatHappened: At 2026-08-19 17:14:20Z, IAM user jane.smith (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:user/jane.smith) successfully signed into the AWS console from 198.51.100.22 using a Mac browser; CloudTrail records SessionMfaAuthenticated=true and MFAUsed=Yes. The same identity/address made successful CLI DescribeInstances (16:51:50), ListBuckets (16:52:23; response names corp-data-prod), DescribeTrails (17:06:05), ListUsers (17:07:20), and DescribeAlarms (17:20:05) calls. No Jane events exist elsewhere in the 30-day review. Separately, do not conflate this alert with an apparent serious simulated/other AWS sequence: mirage from 198.51.100.42 created backdoor-svc, an active key, and AdministratorAccess, opened a security group to 0.0.0.0/0, launched five instances, read listed sensitive S3 objects, and stopped/deleted CloudTrail; backdoor-svc subsequently logged in from 203.0.113.77.
keyEvidence: CloudTrail ConsoleLogin at 2026-08-19 17:14:20.057Z for jane.smith from 198.51.100.22 succeeded; SessionMfaAuthenticated=true, AdditionalEventData.MFAUsed=Yes, and the browser UA is Mac OS X 14.3.

For jane.smith, the 30-day CloudTrail aggregation returned exactly six events, all from 198.51.100.22, all MFA=true: DescribeInstances, ListBuckets, DescribeTrails, ListUsers, ConsoleLogin, and DescribeAlarms. No write, IAM-change, access-key, or object-read event was recorded for Jane.
RFC 5737 §3 identifies 198.51.100.0/24 as TEST-NET-2, reserved for documentation: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5737. The observed source 198.51.100.22 is within that block.

The 16:00-20:00 CloudTrail review also contains 198.51.100.42 and 203.0.113.50/.77, other RFC 5737 documentation addresses, plus conspicuously example-style AWS IDs. This supports a synthetic/lab interpretation of the source-address alert.

The same time-window review found unrelated mirage activity that successfully created and privileged backdoor-svc, altered network/compute resources, accessed named sensitive S3 objects, and stopped/deleted the trail; it is not attributable to jane.smith.
researchDone: Retrieved AWSCloudTrail schema and queried the exact alert window for jane.smith and 198.51.100.22, including CloudTrail MFA, response, request, and user-agent fields.
Reviewed 30 days of CloudTrail for Jane and for 198.51.100.22; each search returned only the same six Jane events on 2026-08-19.

Reviewed all AWS CloudTrail activity from 16:00-20:00Z and a 30-day set of IAM, CloudTrail, S3-policy, network, compute, credential, and role-change event names. Jane had no such change events; the review exposed a separate mirage/backdoor-svc sequence.
Searched Okta events for jane.smith or 198.51.100.22 across 2026-08-18 through 2026-08-20; no corroborating Okta records were returned.
Searched SecurityAlert for Jane or 198.51.100.22 across 30 days; only this scheduled alert was returned.
Checked the IP allocation against RFC 5737 (IETF Datatracker); 198.51.100.0/24 is TEST-NET-2 documentation space.
